final_description:
Activate for Qdrant RAM exhaustion and memory scaling problems. This skill covers: OOM crashes and nodes being killed by the OS, HNSW indexes consuming most available memory, calculating RAM requirements before scaling to tens or hundreds of millions of vectors, choosing between mmap and in-memory storage, selecting quantization methods (scalar, 4-bit, binary) to compress vector memory footprint, and fitting more vectors onto fixed hardware without provisioning larger machines.

Also use when memory usage is growing unsustainably relative to user or vector count growth.

Skip for: writing Qdrant client code, initial cluster setup, backup/snapshot configuration, embedding model selection, search recall tuning.

history.description:
Use this skill whenever someone has a Qdrant memory problem or memory-related scaling question. Triggers include: OOM crashes or nodes being killed, HNSW index consuming too much RAM, estimating how much memory is needed for a given vector count and dimensions, trying to fit more vectors onto existing hardware without buying bigger machines, deciding between mmap and in-RAM storage, choosing a quantization method (scalar, binary, 4-bit, etc.), or memory usage growing unsustainably as a collection scales. Also use when someone is planning ahead for vector count growth and worried about RAM costs.

Do NOT use for: initial Qdrant cluster setup, writing API client code, backup and snapshot configuration, choosing between embedding models, search recall or accuracy tuning, or comparing Qdrant to other vector databases.
